title: Multi-Stage Architecture: Visual Guide
outline: 1. The Recall Ceiling | the bridge from IR 201's ANN recall and IR 104's precision@k/recall@k: five relevant chunks toggled in or out of a 200-item candidate set, against three reranker qualities | candidate recall r/R is a hard ceiling on recall@k at every later cutoff, so early false negatives are permanent while early false positives can be removed later

2. Contract At Each Stage | the five-stage funnel 1,000 to 300 to 100 to 30 to 10 as tappable rows, each with its contract, plus a toggle for whether source ranks and scores are carried forward | every transition needs input width, output width, score meaning, timeout, fallback, filters and IDs, and without the preserved source ranks you cannot tell a document that entered low everywhere from one fusion damaged

3. The Depth Frontier | the measured sweep of candidate depth 20/50/100/200 against success rate and rerank p95, with a draggable latency allocation and a switchable quality floor | the right budget is the smallest depth clearing both the quality floor and the latency allocation, and the marginal gain per extra candidate collapses from 0.0017 to 0.00005 across that range

4. What Eats The Budget | three dials on the same budget: BM25/dense source overlap shrinking the union, post-filter eligibility turning 50 retrieved into 5 reranked, and QPS times depth turning into pair throughput and replicas | a configured budget is not the delivered budget, because sources overlap, filters run late, and per-request depth multiplies into fleet size
